title: Pasting lemma for cartesian squares of schemes
statement:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{a}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{b}&Y\\
h'\downarrow&&\downarrow h\\
Z'&\xrightarrow{c}&Z
\end{array}
$$

be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes ($fa=bf'$, $hb=ch'$) in which the lower square is cartesian, i.e. $(Y',b,h')$ is a fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $h$ and $c$. Then the upper square is cartesian ($(X',a,f')$ is a fibre product of $f$ and $b$) if and only if the outer rectangle is cartesian ($(X',a,h'f')$ is a fibre product of $hf$ and $c$).
